html:
Makuria was a Christian kingdom of Nubia on the middle Nile, in today's northern Sudan and southern Egypt, with its capital at Old Dongola. On the map it appears from 500 to 1400; the chart covers it as Christian Nubia.

It took shape after the fall of Kush, in the 300s to 500s, and was one of three Nubian kingdoms, with Nobatia to the north and Alodia to the south. Its rulers turned Christian in the mid 500s, as Nobatia had shortly before, and probably in the early 600s Makuria absorbed Nobatia.

In 652 an Arab army from Egypt besieged Dongola but could not take it. The two sides made the Baqt treaty: Nubia sent a yearly payment of slaves, Egypt sent grain, cloth and other goods, and each side left the other alone. This peace lasted, with breaks, for some six hundred years, an unusual length for a treaty with the early caliphate.

Makuria's high point was in the 800s to 1100s, when its kings even pressed on Fatimid Egypt. Its churches were painted with bright murals, such as the cathedral murals of Faras, and its people wrote in Old Nubian, Greek and Coptic.

From the 1270s the Mamluk sultans of Egypt meddled in its royal quarrels and sent armies south. In 1317 the throne hall of Dongola was turned into a mosque. Arab tribes moved in, the kingdom broke up in the 1300s, and Islam slowly replaced Christianity. A small kingdom of Dotawo lasted to the late 1400s.
sum: Makuria was a Christian kingdom of Nubia on the middle Nile, in today's northern Sudan and southern Egypt, with its capital at Old Dongola. On the map it appears from 500 to 1400; the chart covers it as Christian Nubia.
